title: Marcos appoints Lacanilao as DOTr usec, Noreen San Luis as LTO chief
summary: The appointment of Noreen San Luis and Markus Lacanilao comes after Vince Dizon’s return as transportation secretary

blocks.text: The appointment of Noreen San Luis and Markus Lacanilao comes after Vince Dizon’s return as transportation secretary

MANILA, Philippines – President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. appointed Land Transportation Office (LTO) chief Markus Lacanilao as undersecretary of the Department of Transportation (DOTr), Malacañang confirmed on Tuesday, November 24.
Lacanilao will also serve as administrator of the Maritime Industry Authority (MARINA), Palace Press Officer Claire Castro announced in a news briefing on Tuesday.

Lacanilao led the LTO for just over a year. Prior to this stint, he served as a special envoy for transnational crime and played a key role in bringing former president Rodrigo Duterte to the International Criminal Court.
Noreen Bernadette San Luis will succeed Lacanilao as the new LTO chief.

San Luis, a lawyer and registered nurse, brings extensive agency experience to the role. She served as LTO regional director for the Bicol Region from 2012 to 2020, and for Calabarzon from 2020 to 2023.
In the private sector, San Luis worked for Metro Pacific Tollways Corporation’s North Luzon Expressway as vice president for road safety and quality, environment, safety, and health.
In August 2026, Naga City Mayor Leni Robredo appointed San Luis as city administrator.

Previous LTO chiefs Vigor Mendoza II and Teofilo Guadiz III both faced suspension due to their roles in allowing the continued use of an outdated IT system, resulting in motorists being charged an additional P13.3 billion in fees.
Jorjette Aquino was also appointed as the new general manager of the Philippine National Railways. She previously served as an undersecretary of the Presidential Communications Office.
The appointment of San Luis, Aquino, and Lacanilao comes after Vince Dizon’s return as transportation secretary.
In Dizon’s return as DOTr secretary, he was mandated to shorten queues at the LTO and get rid of fixers, Presidential Communications Secretary Lino Cayetano said. – Rappler.com
